author: Arachadonic
body:
Recently on the forums it seems there is a big debate on what it is maps should focus on, should they be aesthetically pleasing to the eye or be focused sorely on how the map plays? The map devs have already said that they will place an emphasis on gameplay before aesthetics, BUT guys this does not give you an excuse to make, frankly, ugly maps! 

Everyone who strives to make a map should be aiming to have the gameplay and aesthetics good. You cannot have one without the other IMO and what a lot of people don't seem to realise is that it can be small simple things that can help make your map more aesthetically pretty without affecting the gameplay.

Let's take everyone's favourite map "RemovedcausepeopleGotTooCaughtUpWithIt" which apperently has the best gameplay but being honest it isn't the most attractive map. An easy fix to that is simply introduce more block types, as currently its 90% stone brick. Another easy way to make a map look more detailed is to add more detail to floors/walls using stairs, slabs, fences etc. You can do all this without changing the gameplay at all so I don't know why people are so anti-aesthetics!

Here are some block types that I personally think go well together and maybe can help add some more detail to your maps:
  • Stone Bricks (one of the best blocks) go well with cobblestone, most logs/wood and really most blocks.
  • Stone Slab can go with most blocks also very useful.
  • Logs naturally go well with planks and stone type blocks.
  • Gravel (for a path maybe?) goes well with dirt, grass, water, sand and some coloured clay.
  • Sandstone can go with stone Bricks, lapis, glowstone, sand, water, obsidian, logs, wood.
These are just a few of the most common blocks that I would use and love. Don't you see though how you can mix them with most other blocks and it looks great! So next time you decide to make a map maybe go easy on using only stone bricks. Personally I think you should use at least 10 different block types in  map... I mean you have like 100 to choose from so why be scabby with it?

I made this because it feels like it has gotten to the point when people are now just looking at maps that are aesthetically pleasing and going "-1 bad gameplay" just for this reason. This is silly. In order to fully test the game-play you need to download the map first as in pictures some things can look smaller/larger etc.

TL;DR Stop being lazy (ironic since tl;dr). You have 100s of block types to choose from so why use the same one for 90% of the map?Aesthetics do not affect gameplay so there is 0 reason why you cannot or will not make a map with both of these things in it.

replies.author: JKawesome
replies.body: If you add more block types to Quintus, it actually does affect gameplay. If the floor has gravel or sand, it makes tunneling a lot harder. If you like fences and stuff around the map, it makes it so you can't rush as well. Also, there are a lot of hiding tricks in Quintus, which would be ruined by adding more block types. For example, if you're on top of their spawn and someone sees you, you can place stone bricks in your hotbar, run to the back, and quickly dig a hole and bury yourself. You wont be able to do that with multiple block types.

replies.author: Arachadonic
replies.body:
There shouldn't be a choice between gameplay OR aesthetics... A good map should have both qualities. Most of the maps seem to just have good gameplay and maybe that is why we have a current overflow of maps, particularly in Nebula as maps get accepted for gameplay > aesthetics.

as I said though there is 0 reason not o use good aesthetics as it normally should not affect the gameplay at all. We also are given tons of materials to work with so IMO people that use the same block for the most the map are just lazy.

Basically there is no excuse.
